title: Paradise Solar Project launched in Muhlenberg County - NewsBreak
text: MUHLENBERG COUNTY, Ky. (WEHT) — What is empty land now will soon be hundreds of thousands of solar panels that will line what was once home to one of the largest coal mines in America. “Where coal was founded first in the commonwealth of Kentucky will be home to one of the largest solar arrays in the commonwealth of Kentucky,” CEO of Edelen Renewables Adam Edelen. “Fully committed to powering the economy of the future.” Officials say the paradise solar project will generate 62.5 megawatts of solar power which is enough to service around 5,300 homes annually. Edelen Renewables officials say the project will bring hundreds of jobs to the county in just the first year with many more to follow with the opportunity solar brings to the community. “We need to think about this as a massive strategic opportunity to bring prosperity to the same communities that have brought power to our country for centuries,” Edelen said. Muhlenberg County Judge Executive Mack Mcgehee worked in these coal mines for over a decade saying he understands the hesitation for change, but he believes this project will help his people. “When the industries change you got to rebound and go in a different direction, and I think the county is going in the right direction now,” Mcgehee said. Edelen says coal mines in this area powered America through an industrial revolution and two world wars but the county has been hit hard financially as those jobs have disappeared over the past decade. He says this venture is about repaying that debt and reigniting Muhlenberg’s legacy of being on the forefront of energy innovation. “We owe these communities a uniquely American debt, and by bringing the opportunities of a green energy economy to them, we can begin to repay that debt,” Edelen said. Because the solar panels will be built on pre-existing coal mines, officials say construction will not disrupt any farm land or homes in the area. Once ground is broken, county officials aim to have the project complete in one year. For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to Eyewitness News (WEHT/WTVW).
